Attribute: Stand BA, volume, crown closure, stems
Rationale: Denser canopy holds the pheromone plume together; thinner stands admit wind that disperses it [@krawchuk2020; @cartwright2018; @powell2014].
Trees under 25 cm are beetle sinks, over 25 cm are sources [@carroll2004bionomics].
Attack cannot occur where the host is absent; a cell without pine is not a refugium [@cartwright2018].
Flight is confined to 19 to 41 degrees C and peaks on bright afternoons, so sunlit slopes are reachable [@safranyik2006chap1; @mccambridge1971].
Shading cools, relieving water stress and sustaining defence, and cool sites also push the beetle toward a two-year cycle [@krawchuk2020; @sambaraju2021].
Wind disrupts the pheromone plume, so exposed ground should have less attack [@krawchuk2020].
Beetles land without discriminating hosts after wind-borne transport, so sheltered, open ground should receive more landings whatever the stand [@hynum1980; @jackson2008; @chen2017].
The strongest terrain term in the companion study on this landscape, but fitted there against regeneration rather than attack [@murphy2026].
Infested groups gather in draws and gullies, and deep snow insulates overwintering brood [@safranyik2006chap1].
The mechanism acts during dispersal, and no study specifies the interval, so it is taken at the flight period [@krawchuk2020; @jones2019].
A composite of temperature, snowpack, season length and host distribution that this design cannot separate [@sambaraju2021].
